_meta.description: Drug database for PharmacologyEngine. Effects are values at relative exposure E = 1.0 (steady state of a CYP normal metabolizer with normal renal function on reference_daily_dose_mg).
_meta.pathways: Fraction of clearance per route. CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4 scale with genotype, inhibition, induction and inflammation. Keys starting with RENAL scale with eGFR. OTHER (UGT, etc.) is unaffected.
_meta.strength: inhibits / induces use FDA interaction-strength classes: weak, moderate, strong.
_meta.effect_channels: antipsychotic, antidepressant, mood_stabilizer, agitation_control, eps_relief, akathisia_relief (efficacy) / sedation, eps, akathisia, anticholinergic, serotonergic (adverse). qtc_ms = QTc increase in ms at E = 1.0.
_meta.sources: Reference values from Stahl's Prescriber's Guide 8e, Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines 15e, Stahl's Essential Psychopharmacology 5e and the Day 4-7 resident lecture scripts. Effect magnitudes are game calibrations, not clinical data. Verify before treating any value as factual.

drugs.name: Haloperidol
drugs.source: High D2 potency, high EPS/akathisia; moderate QTc effect (Maudsley).

drugs.name: Risperidone
drugs.source: Modelled as active moiety (risperidone + 9-OH-risperidone/paliperidone, renally cleared), so CYP2D6 status changes the moiety only modestly.

drugs.name: Aripiprazole
drugs.source: Label: halve dose in CYP2D6 PM or with strong CYP2D6/CYP3A4 inhibitors. Akathisia is the dominant adverse effect.

drugs.name: Olanzapine
drugs.source: CYP1A2 + UGT1A4; smokers clear ~30-40% faster.

drugs.name: Quetiapine
drugs.source: Sensitive CYP3A4 substrate: large changes with ketoconazole/clarithromycin (up) and carbamazepine (down).

drugs.name: Clozapine
drugs.source: Maudsley: target plasma level ≥ 350 ng/mL; seizure risk rises above ~1000 ng/mL. Levels rise ~50% or more after smoking cessation (loss of CYP1A2 induction).

drugs.name: Lithium carbonate
drugs.source: Not metabolized; renal clearance only. NSAIDs, thiazides, ACE inhibitors/ARBs and dehydration raise levels. eps channel represents tremor.

drugs.name: Fluoxetine
drugs.source: Half-life lumps fluoxetine (2-4 d) with norfluoxetine (7-15 d): inhibition builds and persists for weeks.

drugs.name: Paroxetine
drugs.source: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitor; the most anticholinergic SSRI.

drugs.name: Sertraline
drugs.source: Multiple pathways, so it is a weak victim; mild CYP2D6 inhibition at higher doses.

drugs.name: Citalopram
drugs.source: Dose-dependent QTc prolongation (FDA thorough QT: ~8.5 ms at 20 mg). Max 20 mg in CYP2C19 PM or age > 60.

drugs.name: Fluvoxamine
drugs.source: Strong CYP1A2 inhibitor: can raise clozapine/olanzapine levels several-fold.

drugs.name: Carbamazepine
drugs.source: Autoinduction: half-life falls from ~35 h to ~12-17 h over the first weeks. Strong CYP3A4 inducer. reference dose = un-induced equivalent.

drugs.name: Lorazepam
drugs.source: Glucuronidation only (no CYP), so it is preferred when hepatic function or interactions are a concern.

drugs.name: Benztropine
drugs.source: Treats parkinsonism/dystonia; does not treat akathisia well; adds anticholinergic burden.

drugs.name: Propranolol
drugs.source: First-line for antipsychotic-induced akathisia (Maudsley).

drugs.name: Clarithromycin
drugs.source: Strong (mechanism-based) CYP3A4 inhibitor and QTc-prolonging.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.source: CYP1A2 inhibitor: raises clozapine/olanzapine exposure.

drugs.name: Linezolid
drugs.source: MAO inhibition: serotonin toxicity risk with SSRIs (pharmacodynamic interaction).

drugs.name: Ibuprofen
drugs.source: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance (lithium levels up ~25-60%).
